source.title: Obtaining Adjustable Regularization for Free via Iterate Averaging
source.authors: Jingfeng Wu; V. Braverman; Lin F. Yang

record.tranche_reason: Reports its own outcomes for iterate averaging as a regularization method on image classifiers, including CIFAR test accuracy, but does not test memorization capacity or the mapped training-to-test gap conditions directly.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR classifier results compare test accuracy after training with test accuracy after averaging the same training path. MNIST approximation-error plots compare averaged solutions with regularized solutions, not training versus test error. Theories and citations about generalization are not results about the claim.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether checkpoint averaging approximates regularized optimization solutions and improves classifier test accuracy. None of its own results tests V1–V8. Citations to memorization and optimizer generalization results provide motivation only.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish adjustable L2-type regularization effects through iterate averaging for specified optimization settings, with little additional computation, and report empirical benefits for practical deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses checkpoint averaging as an adjustable implicit regularization procedure; the mapped versions concern generalization behavior, optimization and architecture factors, explicit regularizers, or measured properties of the train/test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model are reported separately. The averaging success probability is tested at four values, with 0.99 reported as best for all three main image-classifier settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Geometric checkpoint averaging raises reported test accuracy from 92.54% to 93.18% for VGG-16/CIFAR-10, 94.54% to 94.72% for ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, and 75.62% to 76.24% for ResNet-18/CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric checkpoint averaging can improve CIFAR classifier test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Without weight decay, ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 achieves 92.95% test accuracy with vanilla SGD and 93.21% after averaging.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Checkpoint averaging can improve CIFAR-10 test accuracy without weight decay.

record.problems: The image-classifier experiments compare test accuracy before and after averaging, without reporting corresponding training accuracy, so they do not establish a change in the training-to-test gap. Each experiment is repeated three times; no significance test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. MNIST results in Figures 4 and 5 report approximation error between averaged and regularized optimization paths, not a training-to-test generalization measure; other optimizer and loss comparisons likewise concern approximation error rather than the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, small-data and excessive-dropout conditions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive mismatch is the experimental comparison, not simply missing training accuracy: most versions can be tested using held-out performance when their named factor is varied. Here averaging is varied; none of the factors or relationships named in V1–V8 is tested. MNIST approximation-error results and the infinite-width conjecture supply no additional version evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels or report their train/test accuracies.
No network width sweep or test-error results around or beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No sharpness or other measure of the training-to-test gap.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Averaged model parameters across checkpoints from epochs 61–300 using a geometric weighting scheme; best tested success probability was 0.99.
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns test accuracy after averaging versus after training. It does not measure the training-to-test gap named by the claim versions.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 1, but this is the proposed averaging method's performance comparison, not evidence for a claim version. Exclude from version verdicts.
